threadId: 883091cc-2a08-433e-a3a5-a3163258fa05 ````markdown # Property B Case Study: From Finite Hypergraph Certificates to a Uniform General-k Theorem Let $m(k)$ denote the minimum number of edges in a finite simple $k$-uniform hypergraph that does **not** have Property B—that is, admits no 2-coloring $c: V \to \{\text{red}, \text{blue}\}$ in which every edge contains both colors. Determining $m(k)$ is a classical problem in extremal and probabilistic combinatorics dating back to Erdős (1963–1964) and Radhakrishnan–Srinivasan (2000). These studies were carried out with ARIS. Their proofs, failed routes, verification practices, and accumulated wiki were then distilled into MathRSI's workflows and Property B plugin. New tasks will evaluate MathRSI v1 itself. ### Offline Reader Entrypoints Because GitHub renders HTML files as raw source, clone or download this repository and open **`case-studies/property-b/index.html`** locally in a browser to browse the self-contained offline reader pages (rendered with inline SVG math and local links rewritten to repository resources): - **[General-k Bound & Proof Reader](readers/PROPERTY_B_GENERAL_BOUND.html)** — Complete analytic proof, baseline comparisons, and parameter tables. - **[General-k Lean Formalization Reader](readers/PROPERTY_B_GENERAL_LEAN.html)** — Formal architecture, theorem statement audit, and module map. - **[Property B Domain Plugin](../../plugins/propertyb/skills/mathrsi-propertyb/SKILL.md)** & **[Knowledge Archive](../../plugins/propertyb/knowledge/archive/)** — Distilled skills, 117-lemma inventory, failure maps, checkers, and Lean sources. --- ## 1. Main Mathematical Results ### Uniform Improvement for Every $k \ge 12$ For every integer $k \ge 12$ and every finite simple $k$-uniform hypergraph $H = (V, E)$, let $B_{\mathrm{RS}}(k)$ denote the explicit maximum integer budget accepted by combining the Radhakrishnan–Srinivasan positive-association initial bound with the exact single-overlap integral estimate on the same slow-recoloring process ($B_{\mathrm{RS}}(k)$ is our explicit combined integer functional, not a single named theorem in the original RS paper). Define the integer gain ```text Δ(k) = ⌊ √(B_RS(k)) / (8 (1 + ln k)) ⌋ ≥ 2. ``` Then every finite simple $k$-uniform hypergraph with at most $B_{\mathrm{RS}}(k) + \Delta(k)$ edges is 2-colorable: ```text m(k) ≥ B_RS(k) + Δ(k) + 1 for all k ≥ 12. ``` The universal theorem is proved analytically and verified end-to-end in Lean 4 ([`Twelve.lean`](../../plugins/propertyb/knowledge/archive/formal/Aris4Math/General/Growth/Twelve.lean), audited in [`ReviewAuditGeneralGrowth12.lean`](../../plugins/propertyb/knowledge/archive/formal/ReviewAuditGeneralGrowth12.lean)) using only the three standard axioms (`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`). ![Uniform integer gain Δ(k) over the combined RS budget](assets/delta.png) ### Individual Lower Bounds for $5 \le k \le 12$ and Verification Scope The table below summarizes the individual lower bounds alongside named comparison baselines from the literature (full citations are in the reader pages; these baselines are reference points, not a comprehensive assertion of current world records) and the exact assurance scope of each result: | $k$ | Named Baseline | Bound $m(k) \ge$ | Gain | Proof & Verification Scope | | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- | | **5** | 32 | **35** *(33, 34 in Lean)* | +3 | **$m(5) \ge 33, 34$**: Complete analytic/computer-assisted proofs + end-to-end Lean 4 verification.
**$m(5) \ge 35$**: Complete natural-language candidate proof + local certificates; end-to-end Lean formalization for 35 remains unfinished (paused). | | **6** | 64 | **67** | +3 | Complete computer-assisted proof + full independent exact rational arithmetic replay + static final review (Grok/Gemini); no Lean. | | **7** | 128 | **131** | +3 | Complete candidate proof + full 424-type independent exact rational arithmetic implementation; no cross-family final review or Lean. | | **8** | 263 | **267** | +4 | Complete computer-assisted proof + full independent exact rational arithmetic replay + static final review (Grok/Gemini); no Lean. | | **9** | 538 | **543** | +5 | Complete computer-assisted proof + full independent exact rational arithmetic replay + static final review (Grok/Gemini); no Lean. | | **10** | 1085 | **1112** | +27 | Collaborator proof and certificates + documented historical replays; no Lean. | | **11** | 2245 | **2275** | +30 | Collaborator proof and certificates + documented historical replays; no Lean. | | **12** | 4633 | **4664** | +31 | All 664,355 author parameter instances strictly verified; independent parameter/trace domain coverage + 20 independent exact rational probability spot-checks (not a full second probability implementation); no Lean. | | **All $k \ge 12$** | $B_{\mathrm{RS}}(k)$ | **$B_{\mathrm{RS}}(k) + \Delta(k) + 1$** | $\Delta(k) \ge 2$ | Complete analytic proof + end-to-end Lean 4 formalization of the universal theorem. Section C.2 numerical evaluations and paper-only baseline comparisons (D/E) are separate scopes. | --- ## 2. Mathematical Insights & Research Transitions Four technical lessons drove both the mathematical breakthroughs and the design of MathRSI: 1. **Closing the Full Quantifier Chain (`Original H → Actual Trace → Coverage → Strict Probability → Coloring`)**: Checking that a catalog of local degree/trace profiles satisfies a strict rational inequality does not by itself prove $m(k) \ge M + 1$. Every reduction step must carry an arbitrary minimal counterexample $H$ through vertex-quotient pair coverage and lock selection (`LockExtension`, `PromotionReconstruction`) into an exhaustive integer trace catalog before applying the probability bound. 2. **Exploiting Shared Global Structure Over Isolated Worst Cases**: In small-$k$ bounds, bounding each lock configuration by its worst-case local overlap fails when high-loss configurations cannot coexist in the same hypergraph $H$. Extracting common bad pairs, degree-sum budgets, and signed repair gates across a shared parent object closed the recalcitrant 24-vertex and 23-vertex branches for $m(5) \ge 34$. For general $k \ge 12$, bounding the clique number of the actual single-overlap graph $S(H)$ via incidence Gram matrices and an intersecting-family dichotomy yielded a uniform reduction in the directed single-overlap count $\gamma(H)$ inside the exact RS witness. 3. **Recognizing Stalled Relaxations and Pivoting**: While investigating $m(5) \ge 36$ (35 edges), adding positional lock layouts repeatedly improved sample cases without closing the domain. Switching to a labeled-swap double-counting argument on states with a unique monochromatic edge closed all $v \le 18$ hypergraphs in one analytic stroke ([`SMALL_VERTEX_SWAP.md`](../../plugins/propertyb/knowledge/archive/proofs/propertyb35/SMALL_VERTEX_SWAP.md)). Because eight major obligations on $19 \le v \le 25$ remained open, $m(5) \ge 36$ was paused with an explicit gap audit—and that pause redirected effort toward the general-$k$ structural argument. 4. **Building One Non-Trivial `actual_caller` First in Lean**: In Lean 4, natural-number truncated subtraction (`a - b = 0` when $a < b$) can silently turn a flawed trace reconstruction into a vacuous truth, and naive large numeral arrays can trigger kernel stack overflows. Proving a single end-to-end `actual_caller` from a bare `[Finite V]` hypergraph to `PropertyB H` before batch-generating certificate modules fixes the exact interface early. --- ## 3. How These Practices Map to MathRSI's Workflow The historical transitions above directly shaped the five subworkflows orchestrated by [`mathrsi-research`](../../base/skills/mathrsi-research/SKILL.md) and the [`mathrsi-propertyb`](../../plugins/propertyb/skills/mathrsi-propertyb/SKILL.md) plugin: | MathRSI Subworkflow | Distilled Property B Research Practice | | :--- | :--- | | **1. [`mathrsi-prepare`](../../base/skills/mathrsi-prepare/SKILL.md)** ([`specify`](../../base/skills/mathrsi-specify/SKILL.md) $\to$ [`survey`](../../base/skills/mathrsi-survey/SKILL.md)) | Re-reads primary sources (such as Appendix A and Claim 2.4 of Radhakrishnan–Srinivasan) to verify exact theorem hypotheses and prevent claiming existing terms as new contributions. | | **2. [`mathrsi-route-loop`](../../base/skills/mathrsi-route-loop/SKILL.md)** | Challenges candidate relaxations with adversarial reviews and minimal discriminative probes; forces a route change when local tweaks fail to shrink the global obligation domain. | | **3. [`mathrsi-prove`](../../base/skills/mathrsi-prove/SKILL.md)** | Pairs derivations and parallel domain workers with an immediate `actual_caller` check so every conditional lemma or certificate connects back to the original hypergraph $H$. | | **4. [`mathrsi-verify`](../../base/skills/mathrsi-verify/SKILL.md)** ([`assemble`](../../base/skills/mathrsi-assemble/SKILL.md)) | Separates domain coverage from exact rational/integer arithmetic (`Fraction` / directed integer rounding), returns scoped local checks to `prove`, and audits top-level Lean theorems against bare definitions. | | **5. [`mathrsi-handoff`](../../base/skills/mathrsi-handoff/SKILL.md)** | Records verified theorems, independent replay commands, and exact remaining obligations (`NEXT_SESSION.md` and `research-wiki`) so paused investigations like $m(5) \ge 36$ preserve reusable conditional tools without overclaiming completion. | When a new agent tackles a hypergraph coloring problem with [`mathrsi-propertyb`](../../plugins/propertyb/skills/mathrsi-propertyb/SKILL.md), it does not start from scratch: it queries the 117-lemma inventory ([`08-complete-lemma-inventory.md`](../../plugins/propertyb/skills/mathrsi-propertyb/references/mathematics/08-complete-lemma-inventory.md)), checks the negative-result map ([`failure-map.md`](../../plugins/propertyb/skills/mathrsi-propertyb/references/practice/failure-map.md)) to avoid known dead ends, and invokes the archived exact checkers. --- ## 4. Reproducing the Archived Lean Verifications To inspect or replay the archived Lean 4 proofs, work in an isolated copy of [`plugins/propertyb/knowledge/archive/formal/`](../../plugins/propertyb/knowledge/archive/formal/) with `elan` configured for the pinned [`lean-toolchain`](../../plugins/propertyb/knowledge/archive/formal/lean-toolchain) (`leanprover/lean4:v4.24.0`) and [`lake-manifest.json`](../../plugins/propertyb/knowledge/archive/formal/lake-manifest.json). Build the explicit target modules rather than running a bare `lake build` (whose default target points only to an older `Aris4Math.Main` module): ```bash # Uniform general-k theorem (k >= 12) and bare-definition axiom/statement audit lake build Aris4Math.General.Growth.Twelve lake env lean ReviewAuditGeneralGrowth12.lean # Complete m(5) >= 34 (T33) formalization and bare-definition audit lake build Aris4Math.ThirtyThree.Main lake env lean ReviewAudit33.lean ``` ````
